items.title: Braiding
Braided monoidal category
The inverse braiding is again a braiding
items.strategy: Replace each braiding component by its inverse with the variables reversed, observe that one hexagon becomes the other, and use naturality of inverse isomorphisms.

items.title: The braiding is compatible with the unit constraints
items.strategy: Insert the tensor unit into the hexagon, then use the previously established formulas that determine the left and right unitors to derive the two unit-compatibility identities and the relation between c_{1,X} and c_{X,1}^{-1}.

items.title: In a strict braided monoidal category the braiding satisfies the Yang-Baxter equation
items.strategy: Rewrite both hexagons in the strict setting, where the associator and unitors disappear, and compose the resulting triangle identities to obtain the Yang-Baxter relation on X tensor Y tensor Z.

items.title: Symmetric monoidal category
In the presence of symmetry, one hexagon implies the other
items.strategy: Use c_{Y,X}c_{X,Y}=id to rewrite the second hexagon as the inverse of the first with variables permuted, so the two coherence conditions collapse to one exactly in the symmetric case.

items.title: Braided monoidal functor
Being braided is a property of a strong monoidal functor
The cartesian swap braiding is a symmetry
items.strategy: In a category with finite products, use the universal property of X times Y to define the swap map to Y times X, check the hexagon by comparing projections, and note that swapping twice is the identity.

items.title: The double-braiding center is a symmetric monoidal subcategory
items.strategy: Take the full subcategory on objects X whose double braiding with every object is the identity, prove closure under tensor product by expanding the double braiding with X tensor Y, and observe that on this subcategory the inherited braiding squares to the identity.

items.title: Every braided monoidal category is monoidally equivalent to a strict braided one
items.strategy: Start from Mac Lane strictification, transport the braiding across the chosen monoidal equivalence to the strict model, and verify that the transported family still satisfies the two hexagons.

items.title: The braid group by Artin presentation
The two-strand braid group is infinite cyclic
items.strategy: Observe that the Artin presentation for B_2 has one generator and no braid relation, so it is the free group on one generator; then use torsion-freeness of free groups to identify it with the infinite cyclic group and exclude sigma_1 squared equals the identity.

items.title: The symmetric group has the Coxeter presentation
items.strategy: Map the standard generators to adjacent transpositions, check the braid, commuting, and involution relations directly in S_n, and prove surjectivity from the published generation theorem; injectivity follows by reducing words to permutation normal forms.

items.title: The braid group surjects onto the symmetric group
items.strategy: Send each Artin generator sigma_i to the adjacent transposition s_i, use the Coxeter relations to verify that the Artin relations hold after quotienting by s_i squared equals the identity, and conclude surjectivity because the adjacent transpositions generate S_n.

items.title: The braid category
The braid category is braided but not symmetric
items.strategy: Use the standard crossing braids to define the braiding in the braid category and compute that on the generating object its square is the nontrivial element sigma_1 squared in B_2, which has infinite order.

items.title: Symmetric coherence
items.strategy: Strictify symmetrically, identify the canonical reorderings of X_1 tensor ... tensor X_n with words in the adjacent transpositions, and use the Coxeter presentation to show that each permutation gives a unique canonical map independent of the chosen decomposition.

items.title: Labelled unbracketed and unordered tensor strings are well defined in a symmetric monoidal category
items.strategy: Apply symmetric coherence to a fixed labelled list of tensor-factor occurrences, so the canonical identification depends only on the chosen permutation of those labelled occurrences.

items.title: Braided coherence fails in the symmetric form
items.strategy: Evaluate the canonical braiding endomorphisms on the generating object of the braid category: the endomorphisms id, c squared, c to the fourth, and so on correspond to distinct powers of the generator of B_2, so braided coherence cannot identify all formally built diagrams.

items.title: FALSE: every diagram built from the associator and the braiding commutes
items.strategy: Refute the claim with the infinite family of distinct powers of the basic two-strand braiding supplied by the braid category.

items.title: The braid category is the free strict braided monoidal category on one generator
items.strategy: Given a strict braided monoidal category and an object X, define the image of n to be X tensor n times and send each braid generator to the corresponding local braiding on the i-th and (i+1)-st tensor factors; the braid relations are exactly the Yang-Baxter and distant-commutativity identities.

items.title: Braided coherence is controlled by underlying braids
items.strategy: Strictify the given braided monoidal category, apply the free strict braided theorem to convert canonical composites into braids in the braid category, and transport equality back across the braided equivalence.

items.title: Two canonical braided composites agree exactly when their underlying braids agree
items.strategy: Apply braided coherence to the two canonical composites and compare their images in the free strict braid category.

items.title: The symmetric and braided coherence theorems compare S_n with B_n
FALSE: every braided monoidal category is equivalent to a strict commutative one
items.strategy: Refute the claim with the braid category: strictification removes associators and unitors, but a braided equivalence cannot force the basic braiding on the generator to become the identity.

items.title: Monoid objects in a braided monoidal category form a monoidal category
items.strategy: Define the multiplication on A tensor B by braiding the two middle factors before applying the two monoid multiplications, then verify associativity and the unit law by repeated use of the braid hexagons.

items.title: Monoid objects in a symmetric monoidal category form a symmetric monoidal category
items.strategy: Apply the braided monoid construction in the presence of a symmetry and check that the inherited swap map is again an involutive monoid morphism.

title: Braided and Symmetric Monoidal Categories - Examples

items.title: The swap map on sets is the cartesian braiding
items.strategy: Write the braiding on X times Y as (x,y) mapped to (y,x), then check the two hexagons and the symmetry equation by evaluating both sides on triples of elements.

items.title: The braid group on three strands and its quotient to S_3
items.strategy: Present B_3 with generators sigma_1 and sigma_2 and the single braid relation, then send them to the adjacent transpositions (12) and (23) to display the quotient onto S_3.

items.title: The hexagon checked for cartesian products
items.strategy: Compute both routes around the hexagon on an element (x,(y,z)) and verify that each route lands at ((y,z),x) by the same coordinate permutation.

items.title: Supervector spaces with the sign braiding
items.strategy: On homogeneous vectors v and w, use c(v tensor w)=(-1)^{|v||w|} w tensor v and check that the parity exponents add correctly across the hexagon and square to 1.

items.title: The two-strand braiding in the braid category has infinite order
items.strategy: Identify the braiding on the generating object with sigma_1 in B_2 and use the infinite-cyclic computation to distinguish all of its nonzero powers.

items.title: Two canonical maps with different underlying braids do not agree
items.strategy: Compare the two standard composites from X tensor X tensor X to itself that represent sigma_1 sigma_2 and sigma_2 sigma_1; their underlying braids differ, so braided coherence keeps them distinct.

items.title: Commutative monoid objects in sets are ordinary commutative monoids
items.strategy: Translate the symmetric monoidal structure from sets with cartesian product into the usual multiplication map M times M to M and verify that the categorical commutativity diagram is exactly ab=ba.
